title: Aristotle Politics constitution classifier with ruler-count and beneficiary binding
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Aristotle Politics III.1279a-b binds two distinct parameters: whether one, few, or many hold sovereign power, and whether rule aims at common advantage or the private advantage of a monarch, wealthy class, or needy class. A finite classifier yields kingship/aristocracy/polity for common-good cases and tyranny/oligarchy/democracy for deviant cases. Its worked counterexample shows why a count-only rival misclassifies wealthy majorities and needy minorities.

source.source_span: The complete bounded classification and its difficulty: sovereign power is one/few/many; common advantage yields the correct forms; private advantage yields deviations; wealth and poverty, rather than ruler count alone, distinguish oligarchy and democracy in the counterexamples.
source.provenance: Humanitext displays the Greek text from Ross, Aristotelis Politica (1957), with a machine translation used only for navigation. The card follows the Greek parameter relations and makes no claim that a target uses Greek political terms.

duplicate_screen.checked: IDEA000444 Aristotle Poetics; IDEA000450 Aristotle memory; IDEA000423 Aristotle Physics; route-check condition/reference/binding results.
duplicate_screen.difference: This is a two-parameter classification with an explicit source counterexample to count-only reading. It is not plot causality, memory search, natural-purpose reasoning, or a target political lexicon.

rules: If scope=COMMON, count ONE/F EW/MANY yields KINGSHIP/ARISTOCRACY/POLITY respectively.
If scope=PRIVATE and count=ONE with beneficiary MONARCH, yield TYRANNY.
If scope=PRIVATE and beneficiary WEALTHY, yield OLIGARCHY; if beneficiary NEEDY, yield DEMOCRACY, regardless of whether that class is numerically few or many.
If scope=PRIVATE but the beneficiary class is absent or mixed, return UNRESOLVED rather than inventing a sixth form.
constructor.rival: COUNT_ONLY maps all MANY cases to democracy and all FEW cases to oligarchy, so it reverses Aristotle's explicit wealthy-majority and needy-minority counterexamples.
constructor.observable_consequence: Changing only BENEFICIARY from WEALTHY to NEEDY changes MANY/PRIVATE from OLIGARCHY to DEMOCRACY; changing SCOPE to COMMON changes the same MANY sovereign arrangement to POLITY. Thus count, scope, and beneficiary each affect the output.
constructor.falsifier: Reject if one parameter can vary without changing any classification where the source makes it operative, or if a private mixed-beneficiary case is silently forced into a named form. The source does not license target political terms or a universal modern classification.
constructor.target_binding_limit: No target word, group, or semantic participant is identified; this remains a source-grounded exploratory algebra.
